purpose: How do two independent groups compare when the order of scores matters?
meaning: Pool six learner scores, average the data ranks at ties, and sum group A’s ranks. Subtract six to obtain U_A, which also counts A-over-B wins with half a win for each tie. Compare it with all 20 labeled three-versus-three allocations under the exchangeable-label null.

definition.setting: Six learners complete a workshop challenge in two independent groups of three. The constructed uncalibrated A scores are 1, 3 and v; B scores are 2, 4 and 6. Drag the third A score v, or apply the same positive calibration multiplier k to every score. Follow the pooled ranks into nine cross-group pair comparisons and then the finite allocation tail.

definition.domain_notes: These are constructed scores for independent groups. The conditional reference assumes group labels are exchangeable under equal population distributions, with every labeled three-versus-three allocation equally likely. Pooled ties receive midranks and remain separate learner identities in all 20 allocations. U_A counts A scores greater than B scores plus half of tied pairs; U_B=9−U_A. The two-sided convention includes allocations at least as far from 4.5 as the observed U_A, using doubled integer scores. This is not an untied exact table or a normal approximation. The empirical pair share θ=U_A/9 describes these nine comparisons; it is not a supplied population superiority probability. A general median comparison needs additional shape/location assumptions. No causal claim or probability that the null is true follows. Positive calibration preserves order and ties; numerical loss of a distinct scaled score is a precision failure. Use v from 0 to 7 points and k from 0.5 to 2.

properties.claim: Pool six learner scores, average the data ranks at ties, and sum group A’s ranks. Subtract six to obtain U_A, which also counts A-over-B wins with half a win for each tie. Compare it with all 20 labeled three-versus-three allocations under the exchangeable-label null.
properties.conditions: Two independent groups of three use the same positive score calibration. Under the declared equal-distribution null, all 20 labeled allocations are equally likely.
properties.derivation: For three A learners, subtracting 1+2+3=6 from their pooled rank sum leaves the A-over-B pair count with half credit for ties. The complementary U statistics sum to 3×3=9. Under the equal-distribution exchangeable-label null, all 20 choices of three labeled learners for A are equally likely. The finite two-sided reference compares absolute distance from 4.5 and includes ties. A common positive score multiplier leaves the ordering and pair comparisons unchanged.
